proposals.statement:
theorem rule30_alternating_step (X : Config) (L : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ j < L + 2, X (-(j : ℤ)) = decide (j % 2 = 0)) :
    ∀ j < L + 1, rule30 X (-(j : ℤ)) = decide (j % 2 = 0) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The alternating row `(10)^∞` is one of rule 30's three fixed points (Wolfram 1986 Table 6.2, crystals item 22). This is that fact in the only form the rest of the tier can use: a FINITE alternating stretch running left from the origin survives one step, one cell shorter at its left end, and -- this is the part that is not just 'it is a fixed point' -- the cell AT the origin survives regardless of what sits to the right of it, because the origin is black there and the `or` in `left XOR (centre OR right)` swallows the right neighbour. So a stretch that is alternating on positions `-(L+1)..0` is alternating on `-L..0` one step later, whatever the right half-line does. Each cell is one `rule30_eq` and a Bool case split; the only friction is that the three neighbours of `-(j)` are `-(j+1)`, `-(j)`, `-(j-1)`, so the index arithmetic crosses a ℕ-to-ℤ cast.
proposals.disclaims: Says nothing about the centre column on its own, and nothing about any prize. It is the engine of column_black_run_of_alternating and column_alternating_shrink and has no other purpose.

route.tactics:
have alt_succ : ∀ j : ℕ, (decide ((j + 1) % 2 = 0)) = !(decide (j % 2 = 0)) := by
    intro j
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with hp | hp <;> simp [Nat.add_mod, hp]
  intro j hj
  rw [rule30_eq]
  have hj0 : X (-(j : ℤ)) = decide (j % 2 = 0) := h j (by omega)
  have hjm : X (-(j : ℤ) - 1) = !(decide (j % 2 = 0)) := by
    have hx := h (j + 1) (by omega)
    rw [alt_succ] at hx
    rw [← hx]
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring
  have hor : (X (-(j : ℤ)) || X (-(j : ℤ) + 1)) = true := by
    cases j with
    | zero => rw [hj0]; simp
    | succ n =>
        have hx := h n (by omega)
        have he : X (-((n : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ) + 1) = decide (n % 2 = 0) := by
          rw [← hx]; congr 1; push_cast; ring
        push_cast at hj0 he ⊢
        rw [hj0, he, alt_succ]
        cases (decide (n % 2 = 0)) <;> simp
  rw [hjm, hor]
  cases (decide (j % 2 = 0)) <;> simp

proposals.statement:
theorem column_black_run_of_alternating (X : Config) (t L : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ j < L + 1, column X (-(j : ℤ)) t = decide (j % 2 = 0))
    (s : ℕ) (hs : s ≤ L) : column X 0 (t + s) = true := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: An alternating stretch of depth `L + 1` left of the origin holds the centre cell black for the next `L + 1` steps. Induction on `s`, one application of rule30_alternating_step per step: the stretch shortens by one cell a step and stays alternating, so the origin keeps reading a black cell under it, and the stretch is long enough to last `L` more steps. The direction that matters: this bounds the centre column from BELOW using only the left half of the row, so nothing about column 1 or the right half-line enters -- which is the asymmetry obstruction 9 says the black side of the centre column has and the white side does not.
proposals.disclaims: Not a prize node on its own. It is one half of the correspondence 'black run of the centre column = depth of the alternating background'; the converse is column_alternating_of_black_run.

route.tactics:
induction s generalizing t L with
  | zero =>
      have := h 0 (by omega)
      simpa using this
  | succ n ih =>
      cases L with
      | zero => omega
      | succ M =>
          have hstep : ∀ j < M + 1, column X (-(j : ℤ)) (t + 1) = decide (j % 2 = 0) := by
            have hs2 := rule30_alternating_step (evolveFrom X t) M (by
              intro j hjj
              have := h j (by omega)
              simpa [column] using this)
            intro j hjj
            have hx := hs2 j hjj
            simpa [column, evolveFrom_succ] using hx
          have := ih (t := t + 1) (L := M) hstep (by omega)
          simpa [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using this

witness.expression: (List.range 7).all (fun t => (List.range 5).all (fun j => ((List.range (j + 1)).all (fun s => evolve (t + s) 0) == (List.range (j + 1)).all (fun i => evolve t (-(i : ℤ)) == decide (i % 2 = 0)))))
witness.range: t < 7, j < 5 -- the full iff on the seed, both directions at once

proposals.statement:
theorem column_alternating_of_black_run (X : Config) (t L : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ s ≤ L, column X 0 (t + s) = true)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ L) : column X (-(j : ℤ)) t = decide (j % 2 = 0) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The converse: `L + 1` consecutive black centre cells FORCE the row to be alternating `1 0 1 0 ...` for `L + 1` cells left of the origin. Why: a black centre pins the next centre cell to the negation of the cell at `-1` (column_succ_of_black), so a black run makes the cell at `-1` white; then rule 30 read at `-1`, with a white cell there and a black one at `0`, is a plain negation and hands back the cell at `-2`; and so on inward, one cell per diagonal. Together with column_black_run_of_alternating this is an exact equality, not two inequalities: the length of the centre column's black run at time `t` IS the depth to which the alternating fixed point reaches left of the origin. Verified with zero mismatches over 3,960 rows of the seed and six random rows in explorer/altrun.mjs. The work is that the induction is strong: solving for the cell at `-(j+1)` needs the cell at `-(j-1)` as well as at `-(j)`, so it recurses two steps back, not one.
proposals.disclaims: Not a prize node on its own; the pair with column_black_run_of_alternating is the vocabulary the two P1 nodes below are stated in. As mathematics this is very small -- it is two lines from Wolfram 1986's classification of rule 30's fixed points, which is already crystal 22 -- and I found no statement of it in the held sources, so call it project-internal shading into known, not novel.

route.tactics:
have alt_succ : ∀ j : ℕ, (decide ((j + 1) % 2 = 0)) = !(decide (j % 2 = 0)) := by
    intro j
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with hp | hp <;> simp [Nat.add_mod, hp]
  have aux : ∀ j : ℕ, ∀ (X : Config) (t L : ℕ),
      (∀ s ≤ L, column X 0 (t + s) = true) → j ≤ L →
      column X (-(j : ℤ)) t = decide (j % 2 = 0) := by
    intro j
    induction j using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | _ j ih =>
      match j, ih with
      | 0, _ => intro X t L h _; simpa using h 0 (by omega)
      | (n + 1), ih =>
        intro X t L h hj
        have hn : column X (-(n : ℤ)) t = decide (n % 2 = 0) :=
          ih n (by omega) X t L h (by omega)
        have hor : (column X (-(n : ℤ)) t || column X (-(n : ℤ) + 1) t) = true := by
          cases n with
          | zero => rw [hn]; simp
          | succ m =>
              have hm : column X (-(m : ℤ)) t = decide (m % 2 = 0) :=
                ih m (by omega) X t L h (by omega)
              have he : column X (-((m : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ) + 1) t = decide (m % 2 = 0) := by
                rw [← hm]; congr 1; push_cast; ring
              push_cast at hn he ⊢
              rw [hn, he, alt_succ]
              cases (decide (m % 2 = 0)) <;> simp
        have hnext : column X (-(n : ℤ)) (t + 1) = decide (n % 2 = 0) := by
          cases L with
          | zero => omega
          | succ M =>
              refine ih n (by omega) X (t + 1) M ?_ (by omega)
              intro s hs
              have := h (s + 1) (by omega)
              simpa [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using this
        have hstep : column X (-(n : ℤ)) (t + 1)
            = xor (column X (-(n : ℤ) - 1) t)
                (column X (-(n : ℤ)) t || column X (-(n : ℤ) + 1) t) := by
          simp [column, evolveFrom_succ, rule30_eq]
        rw [hnext, hor] at hstep
        have hval : column X (-(n : ℤ) - 1) t = !(decide (n % 2 = 0)) := by
          cases hb : column X (-(n : ℤ) - 1) t <;> rw [hb] at hstep <;>
            simp at hstep <;> simp [hstep]
        have hfin : column X (-((n : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ)) t = !(decide (n % 2 = 0)) := by
          rw [← hval]; congr 1; push_cast; ring
        push_cast
        rw [hfin, alt_succ]
  exact aux j X t L h hj

witness.expression: (List.range 7).all (fun t => (List.range 5).all (fun j => ((List.range (j + 1)).all (fun s => evolve (t + s) 0) == (List.range (j + 1)).all (fun i => evolve t (-(i : ℤ)) == decide (i % 2 = 0)))))
witness.range: t < 7, j < 5 -- the full iff on the seed, both directions at once

proposals.statement:
theorem column_alternating_shrink (X : Config) (t L : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ j < L + 1, column X (-(j : ℤ)) t = decide (j % 2 = 0))
    (hmax : column X (-((L : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ)) t ≠ decide ((L + 1) % 2 = 0)) :
    (∀ j < L, column X (-(j : ℤ)) (t + 1) = decide (j % 2 = 0))
      ∧ column X (-(L : ℤ)) (t + 1) ≠ decide (L % 2 = 0) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The alternating region left of the origin is a COUNTDOWN: if its depth is exactly `L + 1` at time `t` then it is exactly `L` at time `t + 1` -- it cannot grow, cannot hold, and cannot shrink by two. The `≥` half is rule30_alternating_step; the sharp half is one line, because the cell that would extend the region is the negation of the first cell that broke the pattern, and negating a broken pattern breaks it again. Why this is the node the tier exists to reach: with column_black_run_of_alternating and column_alternating_of_black_run it says the centre column's black runs cannot be built up gradually. Each black run is CREATED in a single step, and it can only be created at a time when the centre cell is white -- because that is the only time the countdown is not already running. So the whole black side of the centre column is decided at its white times, which is exactly where obstruction 9 says the P1 residual lives; the two arrive at the same seam from opposite directions.
proposals.disclaims: Proves no prize. It constrains where the hypothesis of centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_deep_alternating could possibly be established, and does not establish it.

route.tactics:
have alt_succ : ∀ j : ℕ, (decide ((j + 1) % 2 = 0)) = !(decide (j % 2 = 0)) := by
    intro j
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with hp | hp <;> simp [Nat.add_mod, hp]
  constructor
  · intro j hj
    cases L with
    | zero => omega
    | succ M =>
        have hs2 := rule30_alternating_step (evolveFrom X t) M (by
          intro i hii
          have := h i (by omega)
          simpa [column] using this)
        have hx := hs2 j (by omega)
        simpa [column, evolveFrom_succ] using hx
  · have hstep : column X (-(L : ℤ)) (t + 1)
        = xor (column X (-(L : ℤ) - 1) t)
            (column X (-(L : ℤ)) t || column X (-(L : ℤ) + 1) t) := by
      simp [column, evolveFrom_succ, rule30_eq]
    have hL : column X (-(L : ℤ)) t = decide (L % 2 = 0) := h L (by omega)
    have hor : (column X (-(L : ℤ)) t || column X (-(L : ℤ) + 1) t) = true := by
      cases L with
      | zero => rw [hL]; simp
      | succ m =>
          have hm : column X (-(m : ℤ)) t = decide (m % 2 = 0) := h m (by omega)
          have he : column X (-((m : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ) + 1) t = decide (m % 2 = 0) := by
            rw [← hm]; congr 1; push_cast; ring
          push_cast at hL he ⊢
          rw [hL, he, alt_succ]
          cases (decide (m % 2 = 0)) <;> simp
    have hmax' : column X (-(L : ℤ) - 1) t ≠ !(decide (L % 2 = 0)) := by
      have he : column X (-(L : ℤ) - 1) t = column X (-((L : ℕ) + 1 : ℤ)) t := by
        congr 1; push_cast; ring
      rw [he, ← alt_succ]
      exact hmax
    rw [hstep, hor]
    revert hmax'
    cases (column X (-(L : ℤ) - 1) t) <;> cases (decide (L % 2 = 0)) <;> simp

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_long_black_runs
    (h : ∀ k N : ℕ, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ ∀ s < k, centerColumn (t + s) = true) :
    ¬ IsEventuallyPeriodic centerColumn := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: A SUFFICIENT CONDITION FOR PRIZE 1, in the shape the wall asks for. If the centre column has arbitrarily long black runs starting arbitrarily late, it is not eventually periodic. Why: a run of length `p + 1` beginning at or after the onset `N` of a period `p` is one full period of black, so periodicity copies it forward for ever and the centre column is black from that point on -- and centerColumn_not_eventually_constant (already closed) says it is white infinitely often. The work is the strong induction that carries the run forward by whole periods; everything else is arithmetic. This is the first statement on the board that attacks P1 through the centre column's RUN structure rather than through another column, and it is what centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_deep_alternating is stated on top of.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove Prize 1: its hypothesis is unproved and is strictly STRONGER than the conclusion, so nothing can be read back from P1 to it -- Thue-Morse is aperiodic with no run longer than two. The measured black runs of the seed's centre column grow like log2 of the depth (histogram 1996, 968, 504, 257, 120, 58, 34, 16, 4, 3 over 3,960 rows, an exact coin), so the hypothesis is very probably true and no computation can establish it.

route.tactics:
rintro ⟨p, hp, N, hper⟩
  obtain ⟨t, htN, hblack⟩ := h (p + 1) N
  have hall : ∀ s : ℕ, centerColumn (t + s) = true := by
    intro s
    induction s using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | _ s ih =>
        by_cases hsp : s < p + 1
        · exact hblack s hsp
        · have key : centerColumn (t + (s - p) + p) = centerColumn (t + (s - p)) :=
            hper (t + (s - p)) (by omega)
          have hrw : t + (s - p) + p = t + s := by omega
          rw [hrw] at key
          rw [key]
          exact ih (s - p) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨u, huN, hu⟩ := centerColumn_not_eventually_constant.2 t
  have hcon := hall (u - t)
  rw [show t + (u - t) = u by omega] at hcon
  rw [hu] at hcon
  exact Bool.noConfusion hcon

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_deep_alternating
    (h : ∀ k N : ℕ, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ ∀ j < k, evolve t (-(j : ℤ)) = decide (j % 2 = 0)) :
    ¬ IsEventuallyPeriodic centerColumn := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE TIER'S PAYOFF: a sufficient condition for Prize 1 stated entirely about the PICTURE and not about any column. If the alternating fixed point `1 0 1 0 ...` reappears immediately left of the origin to arbitrary depth at arbitrarily late times, then the centre column is not eventually periodic. It follows in three lines from column_black_run_of_alternating (a deep alternating stretch holds the centre black that long) and centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_long_black_runs. Why it is worth having rather than being a restatement: the hypothesis mentions neither the centre column nor a period, so a proof of it need not reason about repetition at all -- it is a claim that a specific finite word of length k occurs at a specific place, infinitely often, and words-in-rows is the vocabulary of crystal 3 (every word has exactly four preimages) and of the leftward solve, neither of which any existing P1 block uses. With column_alternating_shrink it also says WHERE such an occurrence must be created: only at a white centre cell, which is the same seam obstruction 9 names.
proposals.disclaims: DOES NOT PROVE PRIZE 1, and cannot be converted into a proof of it: the hypothesis is unproved and is strictly stronger than the conclusion (an aperiodic sequence may have bounded runs). The OR-to-XOR filter (crystals item 66) was run rather than assumed, in explorer/altrun_xor.mjs over 4,000 rows: rule 30 reaches alternating depth 9 and is still at 7 in its last quarter; rule 150 has a centre column that is black at every one of 4,000 rows and NEVER exceeds alternating depth 4; rule 90's depth is 0 in its last quarter. So the black-run-equals-alternating-depth correspondence this node rests on is false for both XOR rules -- rule 150 has unbounded runs with a bounded depth -- and the argument is not one that survives replacing OR by XOR. That is the filter passing, and it is the OR in `left XOR (centre OR right)` doing the work in two places: swallowing the right neighbour at a black origin, and turning rule 30 at position -1 into a plain negation. No naive witness for the hypothesis: it is about depths beyond any computable range, and a finite check would be `unchecked` rather than a pass.

route.tactics:
refine centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_long_black_runs ?_
  intro k N
  obtain ⟨t, htN, halt⟩ := h (k + 1) N
  refine ⟨t, htN, ?_⟩
  intro s hs
  exact column_black_run_of_alternating initialConfig t k
    (fun j hj => halt j hj) s (by omega)
